proposal.rationale: C001-CH1 requires unsupervised anomaly detection for Modbus/BACnet networks without labelled attack data, stating 'none of our clients has ever given us a packet capture that contains a confirmed attack' and 'supervised classifiers are useless to us.' Vuk Đukić's published work presents a direct technical mechanism: autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish baseline profiles, identifying anomalies by reconstruction error without labelled attack examples. His framework demonstrates '94% detection rates' with 'false positive rate below 2%,' addressing the company's constraint that 'we have plenty of normal traffic' and need 'something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline.' Transfer of this mechanism to the company's industrial environment remains a hypothesis because published results use synthetic data from a testbed, whereas production success depends on real-world traffic composition, on-device inference latency, explainability to plant managers, and integration with ProtoSense module architecture—factors requiring empirical validation in the company's hardware and traffic archives.

plan.question: Can autoencoder-based baseline learning, validated on ArmaturaSec's real traffic archives and hardware bench, achieve <2% false positives and >90% detection on drifts from normal Modbus/BACnet behaviour in production deployments? Post-pilot conditional industrial PhD research: How do learned anomaly signatures transfer across client sites with different network topologies and firmware versions?
plan.experiment: Establish baseline anomaly detector by training autoencoders on 80% of company's benign Modbus traffic (terabyte-scale), stratified by client site and time window. Validate on held-out 20% benign traffic. Measure reconstruction error threshold that minimizes false positives on real client operations. Deploy inference module on company hardware bench; measure CPU, memory, and latency. Generate synthetic attacks (function code injection, coil manipulation, replay) on testbed; record detection and false alarm rates. Compare against baseline: company's current alert thresholds and public ICS dataset false positive rates.

proposal.rationale: Nexara's challenge describes a systematic failure mode—three of five boards failing radiated emissions at 150–450 MHz—with quantified cost (€9,000 per re-test) and a concrete need for predictive methodology during layout review. Radulović's automated layout scoring tool directly addresses this by extracting geometric features from Gerber files (trace-to-plane spacing, clock routing distance, decoupling placement, via stub length) and flagging violations before fabrication. The proposed mechanism is that rule-based geometric analysis, validated at 83% sensitivity on boards with known CISPR 22 Class B failure status, can detect emission hotspots that Nexara's current impedance-focused HyperLynx workflow misses. Transfer of this mechanism to Nexara's five archived boards and pre-compliance lab data remains a hypothesis: the 83% validation was performed on external designs under unknown boundary conditions; Nexara's specific 150–450 MHz failure pattern, PCB layer stack, power delivery topology, and clock frequencies may differ, requiring empirical correlation between scoring output and Nexara's re-test data. Radulović is explicitly open to joint projects combining academic simulation with industrial prototype testing, and possesses near-field scanning and FDTD modelling capabilities. Proposal: integrate her tool into Nexara's design workflow as a three-month pilot, correlate scoring predictions against Nexara's five failed boards and pre-compliance measurements, and establish a go/no-go criterion (target: ≥75% sensitivity on Nexara boards) to determine feasibility of autonomous deployment. If successful, an industrial PhD research question may follow: optimizing rule weights and thresholds for Nexara's specific board family and frequency ranges.

FreshPak Solutions possesses OTR/CO₂TR measurement instruments and shipment data but lacks modelling capability to translate gas-permeability measurements into actionable film specifications. Proposal: the technical mechanism to transfer is her finite element modelling framework for predicting headspace gas dynamics from film permeability coefficients, coupled with her validated film-selection protocol. plan.question: Can Marković's finite element model, calibrated to FreshPak's punnet geometry and Serbian–German cold-chain conditions, identify a commercially available lidding film that maintains headspace oxygen below critical respiration thresholds and reduces day-9 mould incidence to below 1% by day 14? If successful, does a conditional industrial PhD research question on adaptive modified-atmosphere punnet design for multi-species mixed-berry formats warrant a subsequent longer-term partnership?
plan.experiment: Pilot 1: collect headspace gas composition (O₂, CO₂, RH%) from ten punnets each of three candidate films (including Marković's OTR 3,800 baseline and two alternative grades) measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days at 2±1 °C in-house. Parallel pilot 2: replicate trials under simulated transit (temperature and humidity profiles extracted from FreshPak's archived shipment logs spanning two seasons). Pilot 3: run controlled chamber trials to measure micro-condensation liquid-water accumulation inside punnets with each film at 4 °C and 90% RH over 168 hours. Marković will provide finite element model code; FreshPak team operates instruments and logs data.
plan.metrics: Baseline: current mould incidence rate from day-9 and day-14 inspection records; target go/no-go gate is mould incidence ≤1% at day 14 in all three simulated-transit replicates. Secondary metrics: headspace O₂ concentration trajectory (target range species-dependent); micro-condensation liquid-water mass accumulation (lower is better); film cost and commercial availability confirmation.
plan.companyAsk: FreshPak provides: punnet samples (rPET shells, lidding film candidates), ten replicates per film per trial, temperature–humidity shipment logs (raw data), destination inspection reports (mould scoring), lab access (OTR/CO₂TR instruments, environmental chamber), technologist time (8 hours/week, approximately 50 technologist-hours total over 12 weeks), and real raspberries or proxy produce for respiration-rate validation.
plan.researcherAsk: Marković provides: finite element model code and calibration protocol, model validation against FreshPak's headspace time-series, film-specification recommendations with uncertainty quantification, mentorship for one FreshPak technologist on gas-dynamics interpretation, and written interim report (week 8) and final report (week 12) summarizing findings and next-phase industrial PhD research directions.
plan.dataRequired: Temperature and humidity logs from last two seasons' shipments (recordId format and field names to be confirmed by FreshPak); headspace gas composition time-series (O₂, CO₂, RH) collected by FreshPak OTR/CO₂TR instruments (CSV or instrument-native format); mould incidence scoring from archived destination inspection records (spreadsheet, binary incidence or visual rating scale); berry respiration rate data (if available, or to be measured in-house; CO₂ production rate, g CO₂/kg fruit/hour at 2–4 °C); film technical data sheets (OTR, CO₂TR, thickness, material composition for each candidate). Access: FreshPak lab technologist to grant Marković read-only data portal or monthly data uploads; data custodian approval required before sharing outside FreshPak.
plan.milestones: Week 1: (Owner: both) Kick-off meeting; finalize film candidate list and sample shipment to Marković; download temperature–humidity logs and inspection records to shared repository; confirm berry respiration rate or schedule in-house measurement. Week 2–3 (Owner: FreshPak technologist): Pilot 1 headspace trials under static 2 °C; daily O₂/CO₂/RH logging begins. Week 4 (Owner: FreshPak): Pilot 1 analysis and data transfer to Marković; Pilot 2 (simulated transit temperature profiles) begins; micro-condensation chamber trials (Pilot 3) initiated. Week 5–6 (Owner: Marković): Model calibration against Pilot 1 headspace trajectories; interim sensitivity analysis on OTR/CO₂TR ranges. Week 6 (Owner: FreshPak): Pilot 2 and 3 data collection completed. Week 7–8 (Owner: Marković): Model validation against Pilot 2 simulated-transit data; film-specification recommendations drafted; interim report prepared. Week 9 (Owner: both) Interim review meeting; discuss findings and confirm go/no-go decision on candidate films. Week 10–11 (Owner: FreshPak, Marković oversight): Confirmatory in-house trial with leading film candidate using real raspberries, mould scoring at days 7, 9, 11, 14. Week 12 (Owner: Marković): Final report with model predictions, film specification, uncertainty bounds, and scoping for industrial PhD research directions. Deliverables by week 12: (1) calibrated finite element model code, (2) film technical specification with OTR/CO₂TR target ranges, (3) headspace dynamics predictions under three cold-chain scenarios, (4) mould incidence forecast and interpretation, (5) summary of micro-condensation findings, (6) risk mitigation recommendations, (7) outline of potential industrial PhD research topics.
plan.risks: Uncertainty 1: FreshPak's OTR/CO₂TR instrument calibration; divergence from Marković's prior study may stem from instrument drift—mitigation: cross-check one trial against certified reference material or secondary lab before week 3. Risk 5: schedule compression; 12 weeks may be tight for model debugging and two validation cycles—mitigation: prioritize Pilot 1 headspace data collection; defer detailed micro-condensation modelling to industrial PhD if needed.

proposal.rationale: C036-CH1 reports raspberries arriving with mould by day 9 instead of target 14 days, suspected to stem from micro-condensation and mismatched oxygen-transmission rate relative to berry respiration at 2–4 °C cold chain. FreshPak Solutions possesses OTR/CO₂TR measurement instruments and two seasons of shipment data but lacks modelling capability to translate gas-permeability measurements into actionable film specifications. Professor Jelena Marković's published work directly addresses this gap: her study evaluated 12 films, measured headspace gas equilibrium over eight days using finite element modelling, and identified a film (OTR 3,800 cm³/m²/day, CO₂TR 18,000 cm³/m²/day) that reduced mold incidence by 55% and satisfied multi-species atmosphere requirements simultaneously. Proposal: the technical mechanism to transfer is her finite element modelling framework for predicting headspace gas dynamics from film permeability coefficients. This transfer remains a hypothesis because FreshPak's punnet geometry, rPET shell properties, Serbian source climate, and German destination conditions differ from Marković's prior trials; her model must be recalibrated against FreshPak's actual shipment temperature–humidity logs and day-14 mould observations before film recommendations can be confirmed effective in commercial transit.

facts.quote: Raspberries for Germany arrive with mould on day 9; buyers want 14 days.
We suspect the issue is a combination of micro-condensation inside the punnet and an oxygen-transmission rate that is not well matched to berry respiration at 2–4 °C.
We have OTR and CO₂TR instruments in the lab and can measure headspace gas composition, but we do not have the modelling background to translate those numbers into a film specification.
A good result is punnets reaching day fourteen with mould incidence below one percent, confirmed in controlled simulated-transit tests.
Quality lab with three technologists.
industrial PhD supervision; joint projects

A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control.
Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios.
